A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PDNAC research work. Their main text, algorithm, table, equations and complete Appendices A-G are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 presents an algorithm, convergence theorems and proofs. Table 1 summarizes theoretical guarantees; neither the main text nor appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains a theoretical study. Its added discussion and complete appendices contain no experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the actor, critic, MLMC estimation and primal-dual update procedures are unchanged. The new mixing-time tuning suggestion does not revise the specified algorithm.

E1.justification: Neither version uses empirical datasets or evaluation benchmarks. Both address the same formal setting of infinite-horizon average-reward CMDPs; newly cited applications are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical baseline evaluations. Table 1 retains the same theoretical comparison methods, including UC-CURL, PS-CURL and Triple-QA, after matching renumbered references.

E3.justification: No experimental evaluation protocols appear in either version. The analytical step sizes and loop-length choices in Theorems 4.9 and 4.10 are unchanged; the added tuning discussion reports no conducted evaluation.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, robustness experiments or empirical case studies. The expanded mixing-time discussion introduces no such analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained mathematical bias and variance bounds do not constitute a change in empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains all theoretical rates and comparison entries. Theorems 4.9 and 4.10 retain their convergence and constraint-violation bounds, approximation-error terms and horizon conditions. No empirical results are added.

T1.justification: Assumption 4.4(b) corrects the first policy-score index from theta to theta_1. Appendix F, Eq. (78), replaces the initial-distance term involving an unspecified lambda-bar with the consistent reference 2/delta. These are local mathematical corrections; the theorem conclusions and remaining derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract now explicitly qualifies general parametrization by requiring smooth, bounded policy gradients, making previously stated body assumptions visible in the headline claim. The claimed convergence rates and novelty for general-parameterized CMDPs remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4 expands the existing large-horizon caveat with discussion of slowly mixing problems and a suggestion to tune unknown mixing time using the Theorem 4.9 parameterization. The conclusion adds neural critics and relaxing ergodicity as future extensions. These suggestions are not validated results.

D1.justification: v2 adds qualitative hyperparameter guidance: treat unknown mixing time as a tunable quantity when using the existing Theorem 4.9 settings. It provides no tuning ranges or selection procedure, and adds no code, hardware or experimental implementation information.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly relates its MLMC approach to prior unconstrained work, including newly cited Patel et al. (2024), and adds references on neural critics and unichain MDPs. Application citations also change. The central CMDP novelty claim and theoretical comparator set remain intact.

P1.justification: Localized edits qualify the abstract, expand the introduction and mixing-time discussion, and revise future directions. v2 also corrects wording and adds equal-contribution and acknowledgment text. The main narrative structure and Appendices A-G are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 keeps its structure and entries but gains a longer caption explaining approximation floors and policy-class conditions. Title-page formatting and text wrapping around Algorithm 1 change modestly. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves precision through two local mathematical corrections and clearer disclosure of existing policy restrictions and approximation floors in the abstract and Table 1. Added prior-work context better explains the contribution. These are limited gains: the algorithm and guarantees remain unchanged, and the proposed mixing-time tuning remedy remains unvalidated.
